A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KVTuner research and contain 35 complete, readable pages. The main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original quantization, reasoning-accuracy and throughput experiments in Tables 2–8, with additional empirical analyses and results throughout the appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experiments, including the KVTuner benchmark comparisons, throughput measurements, pruning ablations and appendix attention analyses.

M1.justification: The offline multi-objective search, intra-layer precision-pair pruning and inter-layer clustering remain unchanged. The new kernel suggestion in Section 6.4 does not describe an implemented method component.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same reasoning, long-context, perplexity and general-task coverage, including GSM8K, GPQA, LongBench, Wikitext and the appendix SoftAge analyses. No dataset or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain the same BF16, uniform-precision and KIVI comparators. QServe and TurboAttention appear in prospective discussion, without being added to any evaluated comparison.

E3.justification: Calibration samples, search budgets, shot counts, quantization settings and throughput conditions match across versions. Section 6.4 removes an illustrative throughput calculation, but retains the measurement definition and experimental settings.

E4.justification: The pruning ablations in Section 6.6 and Figures 6 and 10, the Table 1 error case, and the appendix attention-pattern and sensitivity analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Prompt/layer averaging and point-estimate reporting are unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or statistical significance tests.

E6.justification: The numerical results, plotted data and qualitative experimental findings match, including all appendix tables. For example, Table 8 retains 4,652 tokens/s and a 21.25% improvement over KV8 for KVTuner-C3.25 at batch size 64 and input length 128.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6, Lemma 1, its assumptions and the Appendix A proof retain the same mathematical content. The visible mathematical changes concern spacing and typesetting.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about sensitivity-aware quantization, nearly lossless low-bit compression, offline search and throughput improvement.

C2.justification: Section 6.4 removes the explanation attributing layer-wise FLOP-cost differences to KV precision-pair efficiency. It adds that QServe and TurboAttention kernels may further improve KVTuner's throughput advantage over INT8 baselines, extending the efficiency discussion without new supporting measurements.

D1.justification: The implementation information, code access, quantization parameters, Optuna search settings and DBSCAN hyperparameters remain unchanged, including Appendices C–D. The prospective kernel discussion supplies no new implementation or reproduction instructions.

R1.justification: v5 adds the TurboAttention reference and connects it and the already-cited QServe to potential throughput improvements. GEAR's citation changes from Kang et al., 2024 to 2024b only for disambiguation; broader research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: Section 6.4 receives localized editing, including removal of the worked throughput example. Yiwu Yao moves before Wulong Liu in the author list. The remaining narrative, section order and appendix organization are preserved.

P2.justification: Figure 1 corrects 'Patero' to 'Pareto'. There are minor typesetting and bibliography-reflow changes, while the scientific plots, table structures and overall layout remain substantially the same.

improvement.justification: The corrected figure label and added kernel context offer small editorial benefits. Removing the worked throughput example leaves the measurement definition intact. The method, proof, empirical support and reproducibility remain unchanged, so these edits do not materially improve or weaken the paper overall.
